messages.text: Are seeds ready to plant or do they need to have cold stratification first ?

Hello Bob,

If you’re buying milkweed seeds to plant in the spring, you’ll need to stratify them first by storing them in the refrigerator for 30 days.

However, we recently launched cold-stratified milkweed seeds on our website—as the name suggests, these are ready to sow and don’t require stratification: https://lasclay.com/en/products/cold-stratified-milkweed-seeds

You’ll also find a planting guide on our website if you’re planning to buy our seeds soon: https://lasclay.com/pages/planting-guide#spring

Warmly,

Hari
